experiments.checkpoint_mapping_evidence: STATIC_AUDIT + LIVE network metadata. The paper names no checkpoint file (it only says 'Our model checkpoints are available at https://huggingface.co/peng12138/CSMCIR', pinned README.md:130-131), so the mapping is established from the author's own metadata: (a) `GET https://huggingface.co/api/models/peng12138/CSMCIR?blobs=true` at revision cf0c19bb346266c295b4b5772ebf03bd1c4f0467 lists exactly one FashionIQ checkpoint, `fashioniq_tuned_clip_best.pt`, size 2720615859, lfs.sha256 c8812071de0640d647c5ba2a70628b80a3289ee2c47676f7a1b6abaa313fa49e - byte-for-byte equal to the registry's expected_size_bytes/expected_sha256 (models.yaml checkpoint_variants for csmcir); (b) the same repo publishes `training_log/fashioniq_validation_metrics.csv`, whose epoch 9 row is the maximum of the `average_recall` column (python3: max over 15 epochs = 67.16708342234294 at epoch 9) and equals the paper's Avg. 67.17 - i.e. the 'best' checkpoint is the epoch whose metrics the paper prints. Residual risk that the file's bytes differ from those that produced the paper's number is not resolvable without a GPU run; no checkpoint exists on this host (workbench/artifacts/checkpoints/ is empty; the only file of that name found was a 1-byte placeholder), so runtime parity is UNKNOWN.

experiments.verification_evidence: STATIC_AUDIT (no run executed). Paper identity: pinned README.md:1 title `CSMCIR: CoT-Enhanced Symmetric Alignment with Memory Bank for Composed Image Retrieval`; ACL Anthology page https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.216/ (HTTP 200, 50542 bytes) metadata: Anthology ID 2026.findings-acl.216, Volume 'Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026', Venue 'Findings', Pages 4411-4424, DOI 10.18653/v1/2026.findings-acl.216, authors Zhipeng Qian, Zihan Liang, Yufei Ma, Ben Chen, Huangyu Dai, Yiwei Ma, Jiayi Ji, Chenyi Lei, Han Li, Xiaoshuai Sun; arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03728 (HTTP 200) same title/authors, 'Submitted on 7 Jan 2026 (v1), last revised 8 May 2026 (v3)'. The repo's own venue string is a typo: README.md:4 prints '(ACL206 Findings)'. NUMBERS: camera-ready Table 1 (page 6 of the PDF = printed page 4416) row `CSMCIR(Ours)` = 52.45 | 74.81 | 57.70 | 75.76 | 61.14 | 80.98 | 57.07 | 77.27 | 67.17, read both by text extraction and visually; the identical row appears in arXiv v3 (HTML <td> cells: ['CSMCIR(Ours)','52.45','74.81','57.70','75.76','61.14','80.98','57.07','77.27','67.17']) and in the arXiv v3 PDF. All three registry numbers (57.07 / 77.27 / 67.17) match exactly. Two paper-side consistency observations worth recording in the audit: (i) mean is self-consistent - python3 (57.07+77.27)/2 = 67.17 exactly; (ii) the printed Average R@10/R@50 cells are NOT the arithmetic mean of the printed per-category cells - python3 (52.45+57.70+61.14)/3 = 57.096666... (printed 57.07) and (74.81+75.76+80.98)/3 = 77.183333... (printed 77.27); the published author log reconciles this: `training_log/fashioniq_validation_metrics.csv` epoch 9 gives dress 52.35498547554016/75.06197094917297, toptee 61.142271757125854/80.97909092903137, shirt 57.70363211631775/75.7605493068695, averages 57.06696311632792 / 77.26720372835796 / 67.16708342234294 - the per-category cells printed in the paper are consistent with that log and the averages are the log's averages rounded to 2 dp. So the registry values trace to the author's own log and to the paper. FINDING (P3, registry): `paper_url: null` and `publication_year: null` (workbench/registry/models.yaml:39 and :36) although the paper is public at two primary URLs; `publication_year` should be 2026, not null. Runtime parity remains UNKNOWN.
